cases.basis: Five physical pages (549, 553, 556, 636, 664) of the pinned gpo-warren-1964 source, mapped to excerpt pages 1-5 by measurements/gpo-warren-1964-suspect-text-excerpt/prepare-excerpt.py, converted and each source raster read against the converted output (tools/compare_pdf.py). This is issue #7's own reproduction path, sidestepping the full 920-page book's separate image-output ceiling failure (#5), not a fix for it. Excerpt pages 1-3 (source 549, 553, 556) are cursive Parkland Memorial Hospital admission notes and a death-declaration statement, confirmed illegible by reading their source rasters directly; both the inherited layer and fresh recognition report implausibleTextLayer/implausibleRecognition and the pages become page-image fallbacks with no reflowed text, which is the correct outcome for genuinely unreadable handwriting, not a defect. Excerpt page 4 (source 636) is a faint carbon typescript whose inherited layer misreads a share of its words in place (implausibleTextLayer, misreadWords), so the page is planned compare: recognized again, and the layer kept unless the fresh reading misreads a smaller share of its own words. What this case pins about that page is the finding — that the library judged the layer damaged and said so — and its page image. It does not pin which side of the comparison won, and it did until #269 and #281: 'and he told me about the things at', 'At 6:00 PM I instructed the officers to bring' and the absence of the discarded layer's 'ftboot' were pinned from a run in which the recognition won. That comparison is decided by a five-point margin between the reading's misread share and the layer's 23.8%, and the reading is Vision's, which is not stable from one run of one binary to the next (#173, #284): the same bytes on the same host fell on both sides of it, and the lane reported FAIL for a condition of the host. The evidence itself is not lost, only moved to where it can be replayed: `aMisreadCarbonTypescriptIsReplacedByARecognitionThatReadsBetter` puts this page's own captured layer and a captured recognition of it through RecognitionPolicy and holds both phrases, the absent token and the ocrUsed warning, the way #173's recognized tables are replayed from captures rather than re-measured. Excerpt page 5 (source 664) is a clean typewritten exhibit whose inherited layer is nonetheless heavily misread (implausibleTextLayer, misreadWords); recognition ran but did not read better (readsBetter false), so the layer was kept instead of replaced (no ocrUsed) -- confirmed by reading the kept, still-garbled text as a corrupted rendering of the same clearly-legible source content, not something else. Not pinned: exact text on pages 1, 2, 3 and 5 (illegible handwriting or an intentionally garbled kept layer, not stable prose to assert), and any claim about the excluded full 920-page book.

Pages 1, 6, 9, 15, 19 and 24 converted and read against the actual output (source rasters for pages 1 and 24 via tools/compare_pdf.py; pages 6, 9, 15 and 19 are prose already reviewed by reading the converted text itself, which is unambiguous). This corpus case, and the ports it gates, now cover all five of #186's upstream fixes: the heading-size threshold on thin-text pages (documentBody floor and the lowercase-standalone-heading exclusion), lexicon-decided line-end hyphens, a bold sub-heading whose paragraph opens past an intervening picture and caption (#218), dingbat font reading and letter-case glyph disagreement (#217, closed by GlyphIdentityReader.swift, a narrowly-scoped content-stream evidence reader in the mold of NativeSpacingReader). Page 1's cover title ('Keeping Our'/'Troops Safe'/'From Insects', three headings) is confirmed unaffected by the new document-body floor; the lowercase cross-reference line 'pages 2, 4-14' beneath it, previously a fourth heading, is confirmed now a paragraph. Page 24's mailing panel (five short lines, previously headings on a page with almost no running text) is confirmed now paragraphs; its 'Visit us at ars.usda.gov/ar' line now reads the dingbat bullet immediately after it as a black circle (U+25CF) rather than a lowercase 'l', confirmed against the source render (a Monotype Sorts glyph, code 79, embedded as WVUHWN+MonotypeSorts). Page 15's photo credit, previously 'BRAD FRITz' (a WVUHWN+Helvetica-Condensed glyph whose ToUnicode map reports code 0x5A as lower-case 'z' while the font's own WinAnsiEncoding, its Nonsymbolic descriptor flags and its CharSet (listing 'Z', not 'z') all agree the glyph drawn is a capital), now reads 'BRAD FRITZ'. Page 9's 'Fighting Filth Flies' sidebar title (nine-point Helvetica-Bold over a ten-and-a-half-point body, with a photograph and its caption between the title and the paragraph it opens) is confirmed now a heading, and its own paragraph ('Nonbiting flies that shuttle between filth...') is confirmed still present as a paragraph in the output; the two are not adjacent in the converted reading order because this page's three columns interleave (#153, pre-existing and out of #218's scope), so this contract checks the heading and the paragraph's presence separately rather than their adjacency (Swift fixture tests cover the direct adjacency on a single-column synthetic page, and against this exact real page in isolation). Pages 6 and 19 each print an ordinary English compound broken across a line end that the book itself never prints whole ('com-panies', 'infec-tions'); both are confirmed joined without a hyphen. A third instance on page 15 ('compli-ance') is not fixed and not pinned: its two halves land in separate paragraph blocks (unrelated column-interleaving behavior, not a hyphen-join question at all) before the hyphen logic ever sees them. Porting the hyphen fix required one adaptation beyond the upstream design: main's simpler addVocabulary (unlike the reference design's opensBrokenWord-aware version) counts a line-initial hyphen-broken fragment (bare 'panies') as if it were an independent vocabulary word, which would otherwise block the lexicon vouch by making both halves look like real standalone words; the ported lexiconVouches consults only the system lexicon for that half-word check, never the book's own vocabulary, avoiding the false positive while still protecting a genuine compound like camera-man (both halves are common lexicon words either way). Porting the glyph-identity and sub-heading fixes needed no such adaptation: both are new, self-contained infrastructure with no prior design to diverge from. Not pinned: anything on pages 2-5, 7-8, 10-14, 16-18, 20-23 (most page text is held in preserved-region crops per #158, and column interleaving per #153, both pre-existing and outside this port's scope), and page 24's images (owner rights clearance requires no committed raster or crop from that page; this contract adds no imageRegions or minimumImages check anywhere, matching that constraint).
